wikipedia#0.title: 2006: Gol Transportes Aéreos Flight 1907 collided in mid-air with an Embraer Legacy business jet near Peixoto de Azevedo, Brazil, killing 154 people and triggering a national aviation crisis.

wikipedia#1.title: 2005: John Roberts became the 17th Chief Justice of the United States; he would be the first Chief Justice to serve for twenty years since Melville Fuller in 1908.

wikipedia#2.title: 2004: Archaeologists and volunteers began excavation of the remains of Fort Tanjong Katong in Singapore.

wikipedia#3.title: 1991: The award-winning Disney animated film Beauty and the Beast premiered while unfinished at the New York Film Festival.

wikipedia#4.title: 1990: The Lockheed YF-22, the prototype for the F-22 Raptor, made its first flight.

wikipedia#5.title: 1964: Mafalda, a popular comic strip by Quino, was first published in newspapers in Argentina.

wikipedia#6.title: 1963: The University of East Anglia (coat of arms featured) was founded in Norwich, England, after talk of establishing a university in the city began as early as the 19th century.

wikipedia#7.title: 1957: An explosion at the Soviet nuclear reprocessing plant Mayak released 74 to 1,850 PBq of radioactive material.

wikipedia#8.title: 1955: The first Indonesian legislative election resulted in an unexpectedly poor result for the Masyumi Party of incumbent prime minister Burhanuddin Harahap (pictured).

wikipedia#9.title: 1954: Willie Mays (pictured) of the New York Giants made The Catch, one of the most famous defensive plays in the history of Major League Baseball.

wikipedia#10.title: 1941: The Holocaust: Nazi forces, aided by Ukrainian collaborators, began a massacre of Jews in a ravine in Kyiv, killing more than 30,000 civilians in two days and thousands more in the following months.

wikipedia#11.title: 1940: During a Royal Australian Air Force training exercise over Brocklesby, two planes collided and interlocked in mid-air (pictured); the pilot of the upper plane was able to land safely using the lower plane's engines.

wikipedia#12.title: 1923: The Mandate for Palestine came into effect, officially creating the protectorates of Mandatory Palestine under British administration and Transjordan as a separate emirate under King Abdullah I.

wikipedia#13.title: 1918: World War I: The Battle of St Quentin Canal took place, which led to the British Fourth Army making the first breach of the German defensive Hindenburg Line.

wikipedia#14.title: 1833: The Spanish American wars of independence ended with the death of King Ferdinand VII, with what had once been the Spanish Empire disintegrating into independent Latin American states.

wikipedia#15.title: 1760: The Williamsburg Bray School, the oldest-surviving school building in the U.S. dedicated to educating Black children, opened at Benjamin Franklin's suggestion.

wikipedia#16.title: 1726: Johann Sebastian Bach led the first performance of Es erhub sich ein Streit, a cantata for Michaelmas.

wikipedia#17.title: 1724: J. S. Bach led the first performance of Herr Gott, dich loben alle wir, BWV 130, based on Paul Eber's hymn in twelve stanzas, for the feast of archangel Michael.

wikipedia#18.title: 1011: An army of Viking pirates that had besieged the English city of Canterbury for weeks took Archbishop Ælfheah prisoner and seized power.
